prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-25. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.42 |
| Retained earnings       | 261,693M |
| Current liabilities     | 2,559,605M |
| Current assets          | 1,067,083M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 303,243M |
| Total liabilities       | 3,107,151M |
| Total assets            | 3,410,394M |
| EBIT / operating income | 12,435M |
| Revenue                 | 49,691M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-25, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The provided data show acute liquidity stress (current ratio of 0.42) together with extreme leverage (book equity of only ~9 % of total assets and total liabilities ~91 % of assets). Profitability is also negligible relative to the balance-sheet size (EBIT/TA ≈ 0.36 %), producing a deeply distressed Altman Z-score well below the 1.8 solvency threshold. These metrics collectively map to a rating in the lower tail of the CCC category.
DECISION: CCC
(The data are also consistent with a large financial intermediary, for which conventional non-bank ratios are less diagnostic, but the combination of near-zero ROA and acute maturity mismatch still precludes investment-grade or upper-speculative-grade status.)
